subject: Post-demo: Multilingual evals & model recommendations (EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Multilingual evals & model recommendations (EU / APAC)

Hi Ananya / Thomas —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) What we heard: Globex Retail needs predictable low-latency inference for customer-facing chat in DE/FR/ES (EU) and JA/KO/EN (APAC), plus a monitoring plan to detect quality regressions after model updates. Latency target: p95 < 350ms for 512-token sessions. Budget guidance: focus on minimizing per-token cost for high volume while keeping high quality for the locale-specific prompts.

2) Our recommendation (short): run a two-arm eval: a trimmed open LLaMA-based quantized model for cost-sensitive routing, and a stronger transformer (7B dense) for quality-critical flows. We’ll provide benchmark artifacts and prompt sets by locale.

3) Deliverables I’ll send by EOD Monday:
   - Multilingual benchmark PDF with per-language accuracy, latency & cost (attached: redwood-bench-eu-apac.pdf)
   - Prompt sets / golden references used for the eval (attached: prompt-sets-globex.csv)
   - A proposed mutual action plan and timeline (shared Drive link below)

4) Ask from Globex: please confirm any additional languages or enterprise constraints (e.g., on-prem-only for certain regions, KMS requirements). Also confirm the sample size you want for the evaluation (we used n=500 per language for the attached benchmarks).

Next step: Can we lock a 30-min follow-up on Tuesday to walk the benchmarks and pick the model routing strategy? I’ve penciled in 10:00–10:30 CET but can be flexible.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0130
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick clarifications: 

- Latency target: p95 < 350ms is ideal for customer chat; for batch content-generation routes we can tolerate higher latency.
- Security: for EU payments-related workflows we will need KMS + audit logs, but the initial chat pilot can run hosted.
- Sample size: 500 per language is fine for now; we may expand French & German to 1,000 later.

Two asks before Tuesday: 
1) Can you confirm expected p95 latency numbers from your benchmarks for the two model variants at our expected QPS (we mentioned ~120 req/min)?
2) Any observed quality regressions between the quantized vs dense model for DE/FR? We need concrete failure modes to assess acceptable fallback policies.

Thomas, Hiro — adding you for visibility.

Best,
Ananya
Head of Digital Experience, Globex Retail
Ananya.Singh@globexretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ananya Singh <ananya@globexretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Thomas Müller <thomas.mueller@globex.de>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Multilingual evals & model recommendations (EU / APAC)

Ananya — thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers inline and a short plan: 

1) Benchmarked p95 at 120 req/min (simulated via continuous-batching profile):
   - Quantized (trimmed LLaMA-variant, 8-bit Q): EU languages (DE/FR/ES): p95 ~ 280–320ms; APAC (JA/KO): ~330–360ms.
   - Dense 7B (optimized kernels): EU: p95 ~ 180–220ms; APAC: ~210–250ms.
   Note: these numbers were run on our dedicated T4-equivalent pool; we can provide per-hardware breakdown if you prefer. See benchmark tab in redwood-bench-eu-apac.pdf and Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C-eval-results

2) Quality regressions observed:
   - DE/FR: quantized model shows occasional hallucination on date/time-sensitive prompts and slight drop (~3–5%) on slot-filling precision for product codes. Dense model maintains higher slot precision but costs ~1.8x more per token.
   - For Japanese: quantized variant had character-level split issues in rare named-entity cases (N=12/500).

Recommended mitigation: route high-confidence transactions to dense model (A/B policy), and use prefix/KV caching for repeated context to reduce cost. Also we recommend implementing a lightweight fallback detect (confidence threshold + simple rerank) that switches to dense when the quantized model scores below threshold.

Next steps I’ll take before the Tuesday sync:
- Share a shorter "failure modes" doc summarizing examples per language (I’ll drop it to the Drive).
- Add suggested A/B routing policy config and expected cost delta (CSV).

Rishi / Soojin — I’ve looped you in for monitoring and packaging the prompt sets. Can you prep a short slide on regression detection and alerts?

Marissa

Thanks Marissa / Ananya — brief update from infra/monitoring side: 

We’ll provide: 
- Per-locale quality monitors (BLEU/EM-like heuristics for slot precision), surprisal-based anomaly detection, and per-prompt regression alerts tied to the prompt-sets-globex.csv golden references.
- Suggested retention for eval traces: 90 days by default (we can increase for audits).
- A sample alert playbook: automated rollback to dense model + alert channel to your SRE + an automatic ticket in Jira.

For the Tuesday call I’ll bring: the alert thresholds we used in the attached evals, a short code snippet for hooking our regression hook into your SLOs, and the expected signal-to-noise tradeoffs.

Action items for Ananya: confirm Slack channel for alerts and whether you want DocuSign/contract sign-off before we run the pilot (since KMS for EU payments workflows may push the pilot to a dedicated/private deployment).

-Rishi
